conviction_note: Baseline median reaction is 7.64% and the last two prints were -7.22% and -7.64%; I take a moderate negative because the only company-specific news in the whole capture is Google shipping native e-signature into Workspace in the fortnight before the print, and the tape has run 15.9% higher into it and now sits exactly on the multi-year trendline that has capped the stock.

findings.finding: Google shipped native e-signature into Workspace in the second half of August and followed it with a Google Cloud AI release that knocked DOCU and Thomson Reuters down more than 3% on 2026-08-26 - a direct attack on DocuSign's core product, arriving three weeks before the print, and the stock absorbed it and closed 15.9% higher over the twenty sessions anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: Each Google headline produced a single 3% down day and was immediately bought - the stock is +15.9% over twenty sessions and, per an independent chartist in the same corpus, has pushed into the $60-65 zone where 'this trendline has capped DOCU for a long time'. A competitive event that changes the terminal value of a seat-based e-signature franchise cannot be worth one 3% day, and this print is the first management commentary since it happened. There is no news-search coverage of this ticker (n_queries=0 in all seven sweeps), so no preview weighs the Google launch against the guide.
findings.independence: A second corpus item from a different author on 2026-08-25 records the software complex fading from a double top with 'TEAM DOCU HUBS INTU leading the fall', i.e. the sector bid that absorbed the Google news was already breaking before the print - https://share.trendspider.com/chart/DOCU/66827z0w8p

findings.finding: Insider selling ran continuously into the print with no offsetting purchase: Form 144 and Form 4 both filed 2026-08-28 (four business days before the release), a 144 on 2026-08-07, Form 4s on 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-04, and a nine-filing cluster of Form 4s and 144s on 2026-07-01 and 2026-07-10, spanning exactly the 16% rally.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 144s are unaggregated and the sequence lands in the week before the print. The honest caveat is that DocuSign's insiders sell on standing plans every quarter, so the base rate is high and the marginal information is small - which is why I size it at a fraction of the Google finding.
findings.independence: none - EDGAR index only; no other corpus source references insider activity for this name.

findings.finding: The Estimize crowd consensus sits $0.04 above Wall Street on EPS and $6.98m above on revenue as of the morning of the print - a mild positive surprise expectation that cuts against my other two findings and is the reason my range crosses zero.
